title: Book 6 — Erato, Chapter 136
paragraphs: That was the Pythia's answer to the Parians. As for the Athenians, when Miltiades returned from Paros they began to speak against him, and Xanthippus son of Ariphron especially so: he brought Miltiades before the people, demanding the death penalty and prosecuting him for having deceived the Athenians. Miltiades did not conduct his own defense, though he was present — he was unable to, because his thigh was mortifying — but lay in public view on a bed while his friends spoke for him, making much of the battle at Marathon and of the conquest of Lemnos, how he had taken Lemnos, avenged the wrong done by the Pelasgians, and handed the island over to the Athenians. The people came over to his side as regards the death penalty, acquitting him, but imposed a fine of fifty talents for his offense. Shortly afterward Miltiades died, his thigh having gangrened and rotted, and the fifty talents were paid by his son Cimon.
